title: status.schema.json consumer catalog
content: Load-bearing-contract consumer catalog for plugins/pipeline/schemas/status.schema.json, seeded post-merge of #34 (folds in #42). PROVENANCE, kept as two SHAs deliberately rather than collapsed to one: the three-layer survey below was done at the commit the Phase 4 panel actually reviewed, d8686bc19d317d89d1ec29b8d2cf13c196bb30ff (map.json's basis commit is worktree HEAD 5408339). PR #51 then took two further rounds on top of that reviewed commit -- a nit round closing the two demonstrated AC10 escapes and adding a pipeline.md writer rule, and a post-CI fix re-founding the events/flags discrimination on a crafted tree -- before it was REBASE-merged, which rewrote every SHA. What actually shipped on main is commit 0d0b8d5 (range 1035473..0d0b8d5 on main; on-main equivalents of the two post-review rounds are a2230c1 and b695b6d), released in 0.23.0 as c064b3b. d8686bc predates the events/flags discrimination fix, so anyone diffing at d8686bc sees that cell in its pre-fix, still-broken form; use 0d0b8d5 for anything that needs the shipped state. THREE-LAYER SURVEY: (1) application-code call sites: exactly ONE runtime reader in the whole plugin, plugins/pipeline/scripts/voice-lint.mjs -- readFileSync of the schema at :224, key extraction (properties.current_phase.pattern) at :226 -- and it reads exactly that one key; nothing else in the schema file is consumed at runtime. This was independently re-derived by three separate agents during #34's review (BA, Dev, QA all ran their own grep and landed on the same single reader), which is itself a signal that this fact belongs in the knowledge store rather than being re-earned every run. (2) data-layer-resident readers: none -- this project has no database function/view bodies; status.json is a flat file artifact, not a stored row. (3) independent re-derivations / other readers: plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md is the GROUND TRUTH writer of current_phase literals (the schema's description field is a hand-maintained mirror of what pipeline.md writes, and #42 existed because that mirror had rotted -- 2 stale literals removed, 6 missing literals added, and halted-error correctly kept despite not being a pipeline.md literal because gate-phase-entry.mjs blesses it by name (cite the symbol, not a line number -- this coordinate has now been at four successive positions across three issues, 241 -> 251 -> 312 -> 337, twice moved by the very comment warning against coordinates; re-derive with `git grep -n 'phase === "halted-error"' -- plugins/pipeline/scripts/gate-phase-entry.mjs`) and the schema's own current_phase.pattern alternates it). Three OTHER hand-maintained phase-vocabulary copies exist beyond the schema description and must never be assumed to agree with each other automatically: gate-phase-entry.mjs's exported PREREQUISITES/UNGUARDED/TERMINAL sets, voice-lint.mjs's own VOICE_MOMENTS/NON_VOICE_PHASES table, and dispatch-model.mjs's KNOWN_PHASES. CRITICAL GOVERNANCE FACT carried forward from #34's review: nothing in plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's AGENT_RULES validates status.json against this schema at all, and that walker does not implement maxLength (the token appears once in that file, in a comment saying so). So any constraint written into status.schema.json (existing example: flags[].summary's maxLength:140; new as of #34: events[].verdict and flags[].verdict both maxLength:32) is DOCUMENTATION unless a separate corpus-conformance test enforces it -- see knowledge/living-context/testing--status-schema-verdict-cap-enforcement.json for the enforcement mechanism #34 added. A future change to this schema must state up front whether it ships a reader or is merely a documented writer-rule; shipping neither is the exact defect class #34 fixed for the verdict fields.
